acknowledgementSource: Existing CommandHandoffControl.request two-second confirmation contract; shared end-to-end by local and remote controls, not a new timeout or retry budget.
result: null means no task for this authenticated owner. Otherwise interrupt returns a boolean interrupted and a positive integer pid only on success; background returns a boolean backgrounded. Either may include a string reason. Malformed or mismatched results never certify success.
transport: One loopback connection per control request. A network-order u32 byte length precedes one UTF-8 JSON object. There is no automatic retry or detached accepted-work queue.

semantics.authority: A manager-owned execution incarnation publishes a private endpoint and rotating bearer secret in its existing protected process record. Only the authenticated API owner and exact task/round/tool-call identity reach the existing TaskRuntime command control owner. Hints, file existence and a task ID alone grant no authority.
semantics.interrupt: Interrupt targets the currently live process occurrence by its PID stamp. No request remains queued to affect a later command.
semantics.background: The existing command worker alone transfers its pipes and publishes the background handle. Delivery of a request is never reported as successful handoff.
semantics.failure: Missing or stale execution incarnation, invalid authentication and malformed requests fail closed. Lost responses are unknown and never cause an automatic replay. Existing authoritative tool results resolve user-visible outcome.
semantics.lifecycle: The execution application owns one listener. Closing withdraws admission and joins entered control callbacks before worker shutdown; cancelling a network observer never abandons physical callbacks.
semantics.retention: Only current accepted connections and their callbacks are retained until joined. No durable task state, control ledger or second task registry is created.
